disposition_reason: The text prints concentration ranges for lead, cadmium, arsenic and other metals in commercial brandy, neutral wine spirit and pot still spirit.

study.design: survey of grape spirits from producers
study.origin: South Africa (Breede River Valley, Klein Karoo and Coastal regions; various producers)
study.market: not purchased; samples from producers, compiled 01/04/2000 to 31/03/2006
study.period_text: compiled 1 April 2000 to 31 March 2006; vintages 2001 to 2003
study.method: dilution 10-24x, ICP-MS (Agilent 7900, He collision mode) with internal standards
study.lod_text: LOD per element (unit not printed): Pb 0.4, Cd 1.0, As 1.3, Hg 0.2, Ni 3.7, Cr 8.9, Cu 4.3, Zn 4.6, Fe 42.6, Mn 3.3, Co 0.3
study.qa: internal standard recovery 90-110%, drift monitor 95-105%; NIST-traceable calibration standards; no CRM

controls.control: copper pot still vs column still distillation
controls.comparator: neutral wine spirit from column stills
controls.outcome: maximum Cu 8598.480 µg/L in pot still spirit vs 70.756 µg/L in neutral wine spirit

controls.comparator: unaged pot still and neutral wine spirits
controls.outcome: commercial brandies had significantly higher B, Al, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Zn, Sr, Mo, Cd, Ba and Pb (p<0.05); lead maximum 47.673 vs 9.016 and 0.377 µg/L

regulatory_or_exposure.what: OIV limit for lead in liquor products cited
OIV recommended copper range in alcoholic drinks cited

regulatory_or_exposure.value: 0.02 ppm (20 µg/L); about 18% of commercial spirits exceeded it

unresolved: Mean concentrations are shown only in Figure 1a (figure-only); Table 1 gives estimated daily intakes, not concentrations, and is not used to back-calculate.
Mercury, antimony, selenium, molybdenum, strontium, barium, aluminum, vanadium and boron ranges are not printed in the text (figure-only).

The LOD table does not state its unit; several printed maxima (all cadmium maxima, neutral wine spirit lead) are below the listed LOD, so either the LOD unit differs or the values are below detection.
A zero minimum is interpreted as not detected.
